title: What if neutrons disappeared for 5 seconds? You're in Central Park at...
description_full: What if neutrons disappeared for 5 seconds? You're in Central Park at sunset when every neutron on Earth vanishes. Everything loses half its mass: you suddenly weigh as much as a 5-year-old. But neutrons are what hold every nucleus together. Without them, every atom except hydrogen flies apart. The ground cracks open, each person becomes a 7-megaton bomb, and Earth explodes at 27,000 miles per second. Then the neutrons come back to a world that isn't there anymore... and turn into hydrogen. Which one next? #whatif #pov #simulation #science #physics
title_pattern: 'What if <fundamental thing> disappeared for <N> seconds?' + second-person setting ('You're in Central Park at...'). The caption is the whole script in miniature, cut with an ellipsis mid-scene so the payoff stays in the video, and ends in a comment prompt ('Which one next?'). Formula: tiny, specific duration (5 s) x invisible everyday thing (neutrons) = absurdly huge consequence. Same template is clearly a series on this channel (#simulation #pov).

thumbnail.composition: Default cover = first frame (540x960). 9:16 low-poly 3D Central Park at sunset: skyscrapers top, tree line mid, big empty lawn bottom half; foreground blocky woman with arms raised (centre-right). Atom glyph top-centre, title in the upper third over the sky, HUD countdown at left on the tree line.
thumbnail.text: 'What if neutrons disappeared for 5 seconds?' in a large white book serif (two lines, centred, ~5% frame height) with 'neutrons' coloured amber; HUD: small caps 'NEUTRONS DISAPPEAR IN', big serif '0:08.000', small caps 'EVERY ATOM BUT HYDROGEN HAS THEM'.
thumbnail.colours: Dusk pink/mauve sky, warm grey skyscrapers with lit windows, deep green lawn and trees; amber accent word; atom glyph red/gold nucleus with glowing blue electrons - the only cool accent.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: A single atom glyph floating over a whole city skyline (micro vs macro), and tiny people on a vast lawn - previews the story's scale jump from nucleus to planet.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads as a calm, beautiful scene with a bomb-timer on it: the countdown says 'something is about to happen here'. The question is fully readable at feed size, the one coloured keyword tells you the topic instantly, and the clean premium typography (serif + small caps HUD) looks like a polished simulation rather than a meme, which signals high production value and 'science you can trust'.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [No voice - on-screen text only] 'What if neutrons disappeared for 5 seconds?' (title card 0-4.5 s) + HUD 'NEUTRONS DISAPPEAR IN 0:08.000 ... EVERY ATOM BUT HYDROGEN HAS THEM' ticking down; at 5 s caption 'You're in Central Park, New York.'
hook.device: Question title + live countdown timer (open loop with a visible deadline: the event lands at 8 s, so a viewer only needs to survive 8 s to get the first payoff) + second-person POV placement in a peaceful, specific real place. Silent-text format means it works sound-off. The countdown re-arms immediately as 'NEUTRONS RETURN IN 0:04.958' (11x slow-mo), giving a second, longer deadline that carries the entire video to 64 s.

beats.summary: Title card over the scene: 'What if neutrons disappeared for 5 seconds?' with an atom glyph (nucleus with n/+ particles, blue electron orbits). HUD countdown 'NEUTRONS DISAPPEAR IN 0:08.000' already ticking + fact line 'every atom but hydrogen has them'. Ticking clock is the hook: you watch to see what happens at zero.
'You're in Central Park, New York.' Sunset low-poly park, picnics, a dog; countdown hits zero. Second-person POV places the viewer in an ordinary, peaceful scene.

Neutrons vanish (atom glyph shatters, SFX hit at 8 s). HUD flips to 'NEUTRONS RETURN IN 0:04.958 / TIME SLOWED DOWN 11x'. First consequence is almost fun: 'Every atom just lost half its mass' (dog leaps absurdly high), 'You now weigh as much as a 5-year-old' (HUD: your weight 41 lb).
First-person view of your own raised blocky hands, glitter particles drifting up, people floating slightly. Quiet audio dip; calm before the turn.

'But neutrons hold every nucleus together.' -> 'Without them, every nucleus flies apart.' Sky turns magenta, vertical light pillars rise, HUD 'EVERY GRAM: 100 TONS OF TNT'. The 'But' is the pivot from quirky to catastrophic.
Camera tilts to the ground: glowing orange hexagonal cracks spread through the grass; POV hands over glowing ground, 'Protons shoot out at 15% of light speed.' Scene brightens toward white.
Wide shot: people silhouetted in light pillars; 'Each person becomes a 7-megaton bomb.' Full white-out.

From white, pull back to space: Earth glowing with the same hex crack network, then exploding with a shock ring; 'Earth explodes at 27,000 miles a second.' HUD live counter: Earth is now 9,365 -> 43,883 miles wide.

'It reaches the Moon 9 seconds later.' The fireball Earth swells toward a dark Moon silhouette (lower right); HUD 'MOON HIT IN 7.9 S' counts down while 'NEUTRONS RETURN IN' approaches zero. Two countdowns race; 10 s with no caption, just loud sustained score.

HUD 'NEUTRONS BACK'. Gold point-cloud ghost of the Central Park skyline and people: 'Every neutron returns to where it was.' (CENTRAL PARK, 5 SECONDS LATER) - but nothing is there. 'Alone, they fall in and turn to hydrogen.' (HALF WILL BE HYDROGEN IN 10 MIN). Particles collapse into a swirl, gold flash.

1.5 s of near-black, then the opening title returns as an end card with two small mono fact lines ('Neutrons are 45% of your mass / Without them, the only element is hydrogen'). Title-to-title loop invites a rewatch; caption asks 'Which one next?' for comments.

pacing.note_wpm: No narration. 13 caption cards (~6-8 words each, incl. title + end card) over 80 s ~ 62 wpm of reading; plus a constantly changing HUD stat line (10 states). Captions stay up ~2.5-3.5 s, with deliberate caption-free gaps (16-20 s lull, 54-64 s pre-climax, 71-74 s) where visuals and the score carry it.
pacing.note_shots: ffmpeg scene detection (threshold 0.25) found 0 hard cuts: it is one continuous virtual camera with whip pans, tilts, white-outs and flashes as transitions. Visual 'shots' (new composition/state) change every ~2-5 s; the longest hold is the 10 s fireball push-in before the Moon impact, a suspense hold not a lull.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~4-8 s: each caption is a new, bigger consequence (half mass -> weight -> nuclei fly apart -> protons at 15% c -> 7-megaton people -> Earth explodes -> hits Moon -> neutrons return -> hydrogen). HUD stat changes add micro re-hooks between captions.
pacing.caption_style: One centred line, white italic book serif, ~2.5% frame height, lower-middle (~68% down), soft shadow, fade in/out. HUD top-left at ~48% down: letter-spaced small caps label, large serif monospaced-digit timer with milliseconds, letter-spaced small caps stat line.
pacing.music_sfx: No speech. Score/ambient bed only. RMS per second: ~-25 dB quiet bed 0-7 s; transient hit at 8 s (neutrons vanish); dip to -30 dB 15-18 s (lull); hit at 19 s; steady crescendo from 27 s to a loud plateau ~-14 dB 40-64 s; peak at 64 s (neutrons back), drop to -26 dB 67 s, hit at 71 s (gold flash), fade to silence over the end card 72-80 s.

transcript_source: No speech in audio (faster-whisper small CPU: 0 segments). Transcript = burned-in captions + HUD read visually from 1 fps frames and 2x HUD crops; saved to research/library/transcripts/7693617402180881697.txt
techniques_worth_copying: Two-stage countdown HUD: a real-time 'X DISAPPEARS IN 0:08' that pays off at 8 s, then a slowed 'X RETURNS IN 0:04.958 / TIME SLOWED DOWN 11x' that stretches 5 story-seconds across 56 s. A visible deadline is a built-in retention bar.
Second-person POV in a named, peaceful, real place ('You're in Central Park, New York') plus literal first-person hands - the viewer is the victim.

Escalation ladder that starts fun and harmless (dog leaps, you weigh 41 lb) then pivots on one word ('But...') into catastrophe; each card is strictly bigger in scale: person -> ground -> everyone -> Earth -> Moon.

Live stat line under the timer that converts the abstract into concrete, changing numbers (YOUR WEIGHT: 41 LB, EVERY GRAM: 100 TONS OF TNT, EARTH IS NOW 24,779 MILES WIDE, MOON HIT IN 7.9 S). Counting numbers = motion even when the camera holds.
Racing double countdown before the climax (NEUTRONS RETURN IN vs MOON HIT IN) with captions removed for 10 s and the score at its loudest.
Ironic twist ending: the fix arrives too late - neutrons return 'to where it was' as a gold point-cloud ghost of the park, then decay to hydrogen. Restoration that makes it worse.
Visual motif carried across scales: hexagonal glowing cracks on the lawn reappear on the whole planet, so the scale jump reads instantly.
White-out as a scale transition (park -> space) and gold flashes as act breaks; no hard cuts at all.
Loop design: end card is the exact opening title on black, plus two calm fact lines; description ends 'Which one next?' to farm comments for the series.
Premium, minimal type system (book serif + letter-spaced small caps, one amber keyword) - looks like a documentary simulation, not a meme.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Very feasible in code: it is a stylised real-time 3D sim (looks like Three.js/R3F low-poly) with text overlays. Remotion + @remotion/three (react-three-fiber) covers the 3D; a 2.5D SVG/Canvas fallback is possible but loses the camera moves that carry it.
scene_assets: Procedural low-poly city skyline: instanced boxes with emissive window texture (canvas-generated)
Low-poly trees (icosahedron canopies on cylinders), large ground plane with grass shader/noise
Blocky humanoid figures (box limbs) with simple poses + a dog; picnic blanket with checker texture
First-person hand meshes (box fingers) parented to camera
Atom glyph: SVG or 3D nucleus spheres + 3 elliptical orbit rings with glowing electrons
Earth sphere with emissive Voronoi/hex crack shader; plasma fireball shader (animated noise, orange-cream); Moon as dark sphere silhouette; starfield points
fx: Sky gradient that shifts dusk-pink -> magenta
Glitter/particle system drifting upward (Points with additive blending)
Glowing hex-grid crack decal spreading radially over the ground (shader with time-based radius)
Point-cloud dissolve: sample the park geometry vertices into gold Points, then collapse to a band and a vortex
Full-frame gold flash and fade to #111
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Single continuous scripted camera path with keyframed orbit, whip pan (motion blur via frame-blend or directional blur), tilt-down to overhead, POV mode, and space dolly-out/push-in. Deterministic per frame (useCurrentFrame -> camera pose).
overlays: Title card component (serif, keyword colour highlight) reused as end card
HUD component: small-caps label, big serif timer with ms (computed from frame with a time-dilation factor), stat line with animated number counters
Caption component: one-line italic serif, fade in/out, timed list
code_only_remake_needs.audio: No VO needed. Ambient score bed with a crescendo curve + 3-4 impact hits (8 s, 19 s, 64 s, 71 s) and a fade-out; royalty-free or procedurally generated pads. Optional local TTS would change the format - this one proves text-only works.
code_only_remake_needs.data_driven: Storyboard JSON: [{t, caption, hudLabel, hudStat, timerMode(real|dilated), scene, cameraPreset, fx}] so the same engine renders 'What if <X> disappeared for N seconds' variants.
code_only_remake_needs.render_notes: 80 s @ 30 fps = 2400 frames of WebGL; on the Spark use CPU (SwiftShader/ANGLE) since the GPU is off-limits - keep geometry instanced and low-poly, bloom cheap, and Remotion concurrency <= 4.
